chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from his brother Ja'far ibn 'Isa from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who appointed a woman as an executor and shared the will with her, including a young boy. He said: 'That is permissible, and the woman executes the will and does not wait for the boy's maturity. When the boy reaches maturity, he is not entitled to reject anything except what was a change or alteration; for he may return it to what the deceased had willed.'
2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him):

A man appointed his children as executors, among them are adults who have reached maturity and among them are young children. Is it permissible for the adults to execute his will and pay his debts to those whose claim against the deceased is established by just witnesses, before the young executors reach maturity? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Yes, the adults among the children should pay their father's debt and not delay it because of that.'
3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him):

A man appointed two men as executors. Is it permissible for one of them to take half of the estate alone and the other half? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'It is not fitting for them to contradict the deceased, and they should act according to what he commanded them, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Shia juristic rulings on testamentary execution when executors are minors, women, or multiple individuals?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the rules for testamentary execution (wasiyyah) when the appointed executors are of varying ages or numbers. It establishes that a woman and a minor can jointly execute a will, with the minor having the right to ratify or reject changes made during his minority. It also clarifies that adult children can pay the deceased's debts before the minor children reach maturity, and that multiple executors must act in accordance with the deceased's specific instructions rather than dividing the estate arbitrarily.
